name: SBND
summary: SBND is located on the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam, Batavia, Illinois. This multipurpose SBN near neutrino detector has publicly proposed dark-sector studies.
detection_principle: A near-site liquid-argon TPC provides high statistics, detailed topology and optical timing for beam-dark-particle scattering or decay searches; off-axis subdivisions change the neutrino-to-dark-matter signal ratio.

results.summary: The collaboration outlines light-dark-matter, dark-neutrino and other directions; these are plans / sensitivity studies, rather than achieved exclusions.
Design and initial-performance reports confirm detector data-taking capability; these results are not a dark-matter discovery.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
